sections.overview: Ayres’s black uakari is an Amazonian monkey known from a restricted area of Brazil’s Amazonas State between the Curuduri and Araçá rivers.
sections.identification: It is a dark-coated, robust-bodied, short-tailed Cacajao; field records and measurements remain sparse, so descriptions of individual variation are still limited.
sections.habitat: A few confirmed sightings come from primary forest, including flooded igapó and terra-firme forest mosaics in the Araçá basin.
sections.diet: Species-specific feeding data are lacking; the fruit-and-seed diet of other uakaris cannot be assumed for this species.
sections.behavior: Group size, ranging, activity and tolerance of disturbance remain unknown because the species is rarely seen in the wild.
sections.reproduction: Maturity, gestation and birth interval are unknown; estimates from other Cacajao are not secure species-specific values.
sections.ecology: A 2008 taxonomic revision separated C. ayresi and C. hosomi from the broader C. melanocephalus concept, so older sources may use other names.
sections.conservation: ICMBio reports Data Deficient nationally and Vulnerable globally; suspected hunting for fish bait, low density and no protected-area records are concerns.
